before: A skip link lets someone bypass repeated navigation and reach the main content. Keep this example’s link visible and first in the interactive reading order. A landmark and a fragment link are prior ideas; the new goal is a usable bypass route.

href="#reading" names a fragment; main id="reading" supplies its unique destination. tabindex="-1" lets the target receive focus without adding it to the ordinary Tab sequence. This is useful for a main-content target, not a reason to remove an ordinary action button from keyboard navigation. Never use a positive tabindex here to rearrange the reading order.

```html Skip to reading

``` The first link targets main rather than the navigation itself. In a real browser, Tab to the skip link, activate it with Enter, then inspect where focus and the next Tab move. Merely scrolling to the heading is not the complete focus check. Keep a visible focus indicator; do not hide the outline.

after: A skip link is a shortcut past a page’s navigation links. It helps someone using a keyboard reach the main content sooner. In this lesson, keep it visible and put it before the navigation.
The skip link’s `href="#reading"` must match the main area’s `id="reading"`. Add `tabindex="-1"` to the main area so it can receive focus without becoming an extra stop in the normal Tab order.

``` The first link points to `main`. The named `nav` comes next. `tabindex="-1"` lets the main area receive focus when the shortcut is used. The last link gives you a place to reach with the next Tab press.

before.question: Only the main id changes from reading to observations. Does the unchanged skip link still identify that main?
choices: No. Its #reading fragment no longer matches the target id.
Yes, because the element is still main.
Yes, because tabindex supplies the destination name.
before.explanation: The fragment and id must agree. A main landmark and focus setting do not repair a mismatched address.

after.question: You change main’s id from reading to observations. Will a link to #reading still find it?
choices: No. The link and id no longer match.
Yes, because it is a main element.
Yes, because tabindex names the target.
after.explanation: The link’s fragment name must match the target’s id. Changing one means you must update the other.
